newsitem.title: INDIA: India approves major Coca-Cola investment.
newsitem.headline: India approves major Coca-Cola investment.

text.p: The Indian government has approved an investment by Coca-Cola Co. to set up bottling plants under an overall $700 million investment plan, an industry source said Saturday.
The Press Trust of India said that Coca-Cola's plan to set up two subsidiaries was cleared by the cabinet committee on foreign investment at a meeting on Friday.
Government officials could not be reached for comment.

The approval was one of six foreign investment projects approved by Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujaral's two-month-old government, in a further demonstration of India's commitment to economic liberalisation.

India reopened its doors to the Atlanta-based soft drinks giant after 16 years in 1993. Coca-Cola pulled out of India in 1977 after the government insisted it reveal the formula for its product, a closely-guarded secret.
Coca-Cola's main rival, Pepsico Inc., entered India in 1990 in a joint venture to challenge home-grown cola drinks.

Analysts say the government approval will strengthen Coca-Cola in its ongoing battle with bottlers. It had sought to buy equity in its local bottlers, who resisted on the grounds that the beverage giant was trying to take over their business after having asked them to invest in the plants.
